slides.headline: October 13, 1999: a coalition government was sworn in - and this time, it lasted the full five years.
A 70-member coalition ministry was sworn in at Rashtrapati Bhavan
slides.body: Formed after the 1999 general election, the government brought together more than a dozen regional and national parties under one coalition - a scale of coordination India's parliamentary system had rarely managed to sustain before.

slides.headline: It became the first coalition government to complete a full five-year term.
slides.body: Through 2004, the arrangement proved that a multi-party coalition could govern with the same stability once assumed to require a single dominant party - a quiet but real shift in how Indian democracy was expected to function.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs political stability that doesn't depend on any one party winning outright.
slides.body: A full-term coalition government showed that India's democracy could coordinate across difference and still govern - a capability any developed democracy eventually needs.

sources.text: The Tribune (India) - archival coverage of the October 13, 1999 swearing-in ceremony
